links.comparator_used: Standard chain-of-thought prompting (first answer) vs iterative self-reflection loop, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini
links.outcome: Accuracy on medical multiple-choice QA (MedQA, HeadQA, PubMedQA)
links.effect: Modest gains on MedQA; limited or negative benefits on HeadQA and PubMedQA; more reflection steps did not guarantee better performance; no numeric values in the abstract
links.tradeoff: Self-reflection could introduce new errors or leave errors uncorrected; the abstract reports negative benefit on some datasets but no figures.
links.quote: Our results show that self-reflective prompting does not consistently improve accuracy and its impact is highly dataset- and model-dependent: it yields modest gains on MedQA but provides limited or negative benefits on HeadQA and PubMedQA, and increasing the number of reflection steps does not guarantee better performance.
